saints.name: St. John Chrysostom
saints.title: Bishop and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The "golden-mouthed" preacher of Antioch and archbishop of Constantinople, whose eloquence and courage cost him exile…
biography: Born at Antioch about 349, John studied rhetoric under the pagan Libanius, was baptized, and spent six years as a monk in the mountains until austerities broke his health. Ordained priest in 386, he preached at Antioch for twelve years with such power that later ages named him Chrysostomos, 'the golden-mouthed.'

Consecrated archbishop of Constantinople in 398, he reformed a worldly clergy, founded hospitals, and rebuked the luxury of the court. His fearless preaching made an enemy of the Empress Eudoxia and of Theophilus of Alexandria, who engineered his condemnation at the Synod of the Oak in 403; twice exiled, he was ordered at last to Pityus on the farthest shore of the Black Sea.

He died on the forced march, at Comana in Pontus, on 14 September 407, his last words 'Glory to God for all things.' His relics were brought back to Constantinople in 438, and the liturgy that bears his name is still celebrated in the East. A Doctor of the Church, he is the patron of preachers, whose golden model he remains.
saints.knownFor: His matchless preaching and his fearless defence of the poor and the Gospel.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; Doctor of the Church

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 13 September
